title:
WHO WOULD YOU CALL?
DAMASCUS GATE, JERUSALEM
strategy: The most emotional take in the folder: an old man calling his daughter in America. One take, kept in order. Only two things removed: 3.5s of the 5.5s silence after the first line, and the first of two identical 'Take care and God bless you' lines. Every other pause stays silent. Cuts are shot-size changes (wide <-> close) so the removals read as camera changes, not jump cuts. Project-wide denoise fixed at 14: one take, one location, so one noise floor (LESSONS 41).
beats: HOOK (wide, sign in frame): 'Hello, Shalom Aleichem. How are you, my sweet daughter?' - face + line + the rig in the first second; the question in the title is answered by 0:05
CLOSE: 'I miss you so much.' then a 2.8s silence before 'I love you.' - the silence is the emotion, kept whole. Cut in 0.9s before the line so the long pause still reads as ~2s
THE LINE: 'I hope to see you before I die.' - contiguous with the previous beat (same crop), slow push only here, 1.2s of face after it
WIDE reset: 'God bless you and save you, for you and your children. I love you, my sweet daughter.' - the grandchildren are the concrete detail that makes it real

CLOSE: 'I hope we will meet again. America is not far. Any time we can be close together.' - the distance named; skips the first 'Take care and God bless you' (27.5-29.5) because he says it again at 38s

ENDING LINES (wide): Take care and God bless you. Bye-bye, darling. I love you. (in at 37.7, not 37.6: a 0.1s silent gap keeps beat 05 out of the walk-off framing group, which had aimed its crop off his face)

WORDLESS CLOSE (wide, same shot, no caption): hangs up, sets the phone down, looks up smiling, turns and gives a thumbs-up. Out at 47.6, before a crew member walks into frame at ~47.75 (checked on 4fps frames). Format rule: no CTA, no final caption.
